evidence:
Every criterion (gates, 12 functional, 5 polish, 5 visual likert) was read for an enumerate-then-waive pattern. Most criteria state one conjunctive bar ending 'Fails if any condition stated above does not hold'. Their alternatives are equivalent ways to meet the same leg (hro_interview_places 'Two other ways meet the same three legs'; hro_two_people name/identifier; hro_gate_render 'refusal message is welcome but not required'). Their fallbacks are deterministic (hro_readonly_roles 'A request kind whose own staff control never succeeded ... is left out ...; if no kind has a successful control, this criterion is 0'; hro_candidate 'A candidate page that receives none of its own data makes this criterion 0'; hro_pol_live_board/live_thread 'If no update arrives within 60 seconds ... this row is 0'). Per SKILL.md and internal annotation E34, bundling a whole flow into one bar is not a defect and is not flagged.

INSTANCE 1 (blocking, two targets): tests/scored/functional/prompt.md:21 says 'Where a feature that another criterion grades (adding a candidate, a single move, re-ordering, undo) prevents a step's setup or changes the order a step expects, judge that leg against the state the app actually produced, or leave the leg out and say why; such a leg is not a skipped step, and this criterion is judged on the legs that remain.' This gives the judge an unconditioned choice ('judge ... or leave the leg out') and names undo as a feature graded elsewhere. Yet in several criteria undo is itself a scored leg of their own bar, not setup. hro_interview_places (judge.toml:58) says 'The undo that would overfill Interview is refused with nothing changed; once a place is free the same undo goes ahead and E is back in Interview', the only place the overfill-undo rule is graded. hro_moves (judge.toml:40) says 'undoing the rejection puts C back in Applied at its place' and 'undoing the reopening puts C back in Rejected with its reason', the only successful rejection/reopen undo in the rubric. Each criterion therefore has two full-credit bars. One is all listed legs (criterion text; prompt.md:11 'every leg it names must hold'; prompt.md:33 'A step you skipped ... fails'). The other is the bar with the undo legs left out as 'graded elsewhere' (prompt.md:21). The re-ordering legs inside hro_moves ('A card's place within a stage changes up and down') and hro_interview_places ('Re-ordering inside the full Interview is allowed') follow the same pattern; they are graded bars, not setup.

INSTANCE 2 (same class, lower weight): hro_unread_seen (judge.toml:121) has a fallback for step 3 only ('if Tomas cannot send, which hro_messaging grades, Mei Lin sends them'). Step 5's bar 'Tomas's message shows as seen on his page within 15 seconds ... after Bill opens the conversation, and his next one after Rafael opens it' has none. For an app whose candidate send fails, the judge must choose between failing the leg and leaving it out under prompt.md:21, even though candidate send is not in its parenthetical list.

INSTANCE 3 (note-level tension, P3): hro_moves (judge.toml:40) first permits reading the reason from Activity: 'staff can read the reason and the stage it was rejected from (on the card, its details, its reopen control or its Activity line)'. It then says 'Whether a reason is present is read from the card's current state ..., never from Activity'. Take an app that exposes the reason only in Activity lines and never in a card or board read. Its first leg passes by the explicit allowance, but its 'undoing the reopening puts C back in Rejected with its reason' leg cannot be met, so the allowance never decides the outcome. Scoping it ('the Activity line counts for the first rejection read only') would remove the ambiguity.

Not defects for this row: hro_readonly_roles leaves out kinds whose staff control failed, but the rule is deterministic with a zero floor (one target). That it can leave a broken-write app graded on few kinds is for the floor/coverage rows and is recorded here only for the owner. The polish rows' 'graded only in Functional' and the polish/visual 'Do not deduct the same observed defect in more than one row' scope ownership consistently. The visual likert anchors are single-scale, and each gate states one bar. Colderwater lesson 16 (say 'scored elsewhere' rather than double-grade) motivates prompt.md:21. That clause, however, leaves the choice to the judge instead of naming per criterion which legs are scored elsewhere. There is no configured judge run for this round, so the divergence is shown in the source only (NOT EXERCISED).
counterexample: Take an app that lacks a working undo but follows every other rule. On hro_interview_places (weight 5.5), judge A follows the criterion's 'Fails if any condition stated above does not hold' and prompt.md:33. It scores 0 because the overfill-undo and free-place-undo legs fail. Judge B follows prompt.md:21 ('a feature that another criterion grades (... undo) ... leave the leg out ... judged on the legs that remain'). It drops both undo legs and scores 1. hro_moves (weight 7) splits the same way on its two undo legs. So for these two criteria the same app gets either 0 or 12.5 of the 61 functional weight, depending on which bar the judge picks.
suggested_fix: Replace the open 'judge ... or leave the leg out' in functional/prompt.md:21 with one rule: setup-only legs are judged against the produced state, and each criterion names the legs, if any, that are scored elsewhere. Always grade the undo legs of hro_moves and hro_interview_places and the re-order legs, or move them to hro_undo_activity with a 'scored elsewhere' note. Give hro_unread_seen step 5 a stated fallback or an explicit 0/leave-out rule when Tomas cannot send, and limit hro_moves' Activity allowance to the first rejection read.
